newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia poll irregularities only minor - observers.
newsitem.headline: Liberia poll irregularities only minor - observers.

text.p: Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter and other international observers said on Monday they had seen only minor irregularities during Saturday's national elections in Liberia.

Carter told a news conference most problems his team had seen stemmed from general ignorance on how to vote. "These problems or irregularities did not have a pattern and did not affect the outcome of the elections," he said.
Liberians voted for a president and parliament in elections that are meant to put an end to seven years of civil war.
One of the candidates, former United Nations official Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf, has complained that workers from her party were not allowed to observe the counting of votes in many places.
"In my opinion there is no substance to the allegations," Carter said. If Johnson-Sirleaf had complaints, or had seen any pattern to abuses, she should inform the electoral commission, he added.
Carter's findings were echoed by other observers, including the 52-strong team sent by the European Union.
The EU said in a statement that both polling and counting had been "smooth and peaceful".
"There have been no reports of major irregularities," it added.
The United Nations Mission in Liberia said: "There were no reports of major irregularities, no serious incidents that could have affected the credibility of the process."
All the organisations rejected allegations made by Johnson-Sirleaf's camp of interference in the voting by West African ECOMOG troops who provided security for the elections.
Dismissing the allegations, the EU's chief delegate Antonius Speekebrink told the news conference: "What we did notice was the very helpful presence of ECOMOG."
